newsitem.title: USA: US Senate plans hearing on derivatives accounting.
newsitem.headline: US Senate plans hearing on derivatives accounting.

text.p: With the Financial Accounting Standards Board still working to complete controversial new rules for derivatives, Senator Phil Gramm announced Thursday he would hold a hearing on the matter.
FASB is expected to complete the rules, which would for the first time require companies to carry all derivatives on their balance sheets, by June 30.

Sen Gramm, Republican of Texas, set a March 4 hearing in the Senate Banking Committee's securities subcommittee to examine the FASB rules as well as derivatives disclosure rules adopted recently by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The hearing will explore the impact of the rules on competitiveness and investor information.

Derivatives are financial instruments that are priced based on the value of another instrument, commodity or market index. Common derivatives include an option on a share of stock or a futures contract to buy wheat.
Many companies that use derivatives have complained that the FASB and SEC inititiatives are burdensome and would give investors misleading information.
SEC commissioner Steven Wallman is scheduled to testify along with derivatives experts from academia and business.
